details:
AstraHealth – AI-Assisted Astronaut Health Monitoring & Research Dashboard

AstraHealth is an interactive research dashboard designed to make astronaut health research data easier to explore, understand, and visualize. It uses data from NASA’s Open Science Data Repository (OSDR) as a research reference and provides a structured way to examine astronaut health-related information across different participants and mission timepoints.

The project works by loading and organizing research data, processing it using Python libraries, and presenting the information through an interactive Streamlit dashboard. Users can select participants, explore available timepoints, view health-related indicators through charts, and examine the underlying data in tabular form. The prototype also demonstrates sample CMP (Comprehensive Metabolic Panel) visualizations using synthetic demonstration values. These values are clearly identified as synthetic and are not presented as actual NASA measurements.

The main benefit of AstraHealth is that it makes complex research datasets more accessible and easier to interpret. Instead of manually examining large tables, users can explore information through visualizations and interactive filters. This can support researchers, students, and space-health enthusiasts in identifying patterns, comparing timepoints, and understanding the organization of astronaut health research data.

The intended impact is to contribute to more accessible and understandable space-health research. In the future, AstraHealth could be extended with verified laboratory measurements, AI-assisted trend analysis, anomaly detection, and additional health-related datasets. These features could help researchers investigate changes in health indicators during space missions and support research into the challenges astronauts face during long-duration spaceflight. AstraHealth is a research and educational prototype, not a medical diagnostic or clinical monitoring system.

The project was developed using Python as the primary programming language, with Streamlit for the interactive dashboard, Pandas for data handling, and NumPy for numerical operations. CSV files are used to organize the research metadata and demonstration dataset. The dashboard is designed to be accessible through a web browser, without requiring specialized hardware.

The creative aspect of AstraHealth is its combination of space-health research, interactive data visualization, and the potential for AI-assisted analysis in one platform. Rather than presenting research information as static tables, it transforms the data into an accessible visual experience. The project also emphasizes transparency by distinguishing NASA-provided sample metadata from synthetic demonstration measurements.

During development, the team considered data accuracy, source reliability, clarity of visualizations, ease of use, accessibility, and the limitations of publicly available research data. We also considered the importance of protecting scientific integrity by avoiding unsupported medical conclusions and clearly identifying synthetic data. Our goal was to create a practical foundation that can be expanded as more verified astronaut health datasets and analytical capabilities become available.
